corrections.why: Forest Lookouts prints a bare S after the county with no legend, and no source read names an agency for this tower.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia says the only tower remaining in Pushmataha County is the Flagpole Mountain tower, which implies Cloudy no longer stands. OpenStreetMap still maps a Cloudy observation tower, and a map entry does not show that a structure stands. The sources do not settle it, so status stays unknown.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. The Forest Lookouts page gives only a name, the county and a bare S code. OpenStreetMap gives location, elevation and the observation tag. No source read gives a build date, design, staffing, fires or current condition. The Wikipedia Clayton sentence is undated and its citations were not visible in what we read; it names Cloudy only in a list of the county's other communities and mentions no tower there. The firetower.org Oklahoma page lists no registered former lookout sites. A 2025 Oklahoman feature on southeastern Oklahoma fire towers returned HTTP 403, so it was not read. Agency is set to unknown in the correction because the S code is undefined; the state forestry agency is only a likely owner and no source ties Cloudy to it. Research used 2 web searches and about 4 page reads for this tower, plus shared Oklahoma pages.
